title: VAR Is Watching
pundit_nervous: PUNDIT: Why are you poking around, rookie? Eyes on the football, please.
PUNDIT: Haha... lovely weather tonight. Has anyone seen my lanyard? Not that it matters.
PUNDIT: I want my lawyer. I mean... back to the studio! Quick! Cut to the adverts!

booth.name: VAR Booth
booth.text: 94th minute of the cup final. The home side has just scored and the stadium is shaking. The away captain is screaming "OFFSIDE!" at the linesman, a ball boy and the sky. You sit in the VAR Booth in front of twelve screens. Eleven work. The one with the key angle shows only static. On the TV in the corner, star pundit Rex Smugworth is loving every second. It is your first day.
booth.pundit: PUNDIT: Day one, a missing camera angle and sixty thousand people waiting. Honestly? Best night of my career.

actions.label: Go to the Referee's Dressing Room
actions.text: You sprint down the tunnel, past a confused steward and a trolley of orange slices.

actions.label: Go to the Mascot Changing Room
actions.blocked_text: The door is locked. A laminated sign says: "MASCOTS ONLY. Whistle for entry."
actions.text: You blow the Lucky Whistle. Somewhere inside, a pigeon coos. The door clicks open.

actions.label: Go to the Press Room
actions.text: You follow the sound of camera shutters and bad decisions.

actions.label: Go to the Pitch
actions.blocked_text: A steward blocks the tunnel: "Press conference first, mate. Rules are rules."
actions.text: You walk out under the floodlights. Sixty thousand heads turn. Your knees suddenly remember they are knees.

actions.label: Look at the sticky note
actions.text: Dave's note says: "Back in 5 min - Dave. P.S. If the angle cuts out, ask Pombo. He films EVERYTHING."

actions.label: Look behind the desk
actions.text: Behind the desk, the cable of the key camera has been yanked out of the wall. Somebody did this on purpose! Tangled in the cable is a lanyard: "PRESS - TV STUDIO".

actions.label: Plug the USB Stick into the VAR computer
actions.blocked_text: The VAR computer has a USB port, but you have nothing to plug in.
actions.text: You plug in the USB Stick. Pombo's head-cam footage fills the screen.

dressing_room.name: Referee's Dressing Room
dressing_room.text: Steam, muddy boots and a half-eaten orange. A poster on the wall says "TRUST THE PROCESS". The referee left in a hurry. It smells of deep heat and fear.
dressing_room.pundit: PUNDIT: Snooping in the ref's room on day one. Bold. Pointless, but bold.

actions.label: Take the Lucky Whistle from the bench
actions.text: You pick up the Lucky Whistle. Someone has written LUCKY on it in marker pen, so it must be true.

actions.label: Back to the VAR Booth
actions.text: You hurry back to the booth. The static is still there.

mascot_room.name: Mascot Changing Room
mascot_room.text: Feathers everywhere. Pombo, the club's pigeon mascot, sits on a bench in his giant costume, head in his wings. He was standing right next to the corner flag when the goal went in.
mascot_room.pundit: PUNDIT: The rookie is interviewing a pigeon. I could not have scripted this.

actions.label: Ask Pombo what he saw
actions.text: Pombo pulls off his pigeon head. It's Dave, the missing VAR operator! "Second job. Don't tell HR." He hands you a USB Stick: "Filmed the whole thing on my head-cam." Then he whispers: "At 93:30 a guy in a shiny suit ran out of your booth. Smelled of hair gel."

actions.label: Back to the VAR Booth
actions.text: You leave Dave to put his head back on and run back to the booth.

press_room.name: Press Room
press_room.text: A wall of microphones and flashing cameras. Every journalist in the country wants one quote from the new VAR official, and they want it now. You only get to say one thing.
press_room.pundit: PUNDIT: Just tell them it's offside, rookie. Easiest quote of your life.

actions.label: Say: 'Clearly a goal!'
actions.text: Cameras flash. The headline is written before you finish the sentence. Somewhere, a VAR rulebook bursts into flames.

actions.label: Say: 'No comment.'
actions.text: "No comment." Calm. Professional. Boring. The journalists sigh and put their phones away.

actions.label: Say: 'Rex Smugworth cut the camera feed. Here is the proof.'
actions.blocked_text: You can't accuse someone on live TV without proof. You need to know who was in the booth, why they did it, and a witness.
actions.text: "Rex Smugworth pulled the camera cable. Here is his lanyard, his betting slip, and a witness in a pigeon costume." The room goes silent. Then every camera turns towards the TV studio.

actions.label: Pick up the crumpled paper by the TV camera
actions.text: It's a betting slip: "500 pounds - AWAY WIN - late offside drama". Signed: R. Smugworth. Wait... isn't that the pundit on TV?

actions.label: Back to the VAR Booth
actions.text: You leave the Press Room. A journalist is still shouting questions at the closed door.

pitch.name: The Pitch
pitch.text: Sixty thousand fans are on their feet. The linesman has his flag up. The away captain is screaming. The referee holds a hand to his earpiece and stares at you: "VAR, what's your call?"
pitch.pundit: PUNDIT: Clearly offside! Draw the line on the high defender, rookie. Everyone knows that.

actions.label: Back to the VAR Booth
actions.text: You walk back inside. Sixty thousand people boo at the same time. Impressive, really.

review.intro: The footage has four moments. You only get one look before the referee needs an answer, so freeze the right moment and draw the offside line on the right player.

frames.name: The build-up
frames.text: The home midfielder has the ball at his feet and looks up.

frames.name: The pass
frames.text: The ball is just leaving the midfielder's boot.

frames.name: The run
frames.text: The ball is rolling forward. The striker sprints past the defenders.

frames.name: The goal
frames.text: The ball hits the back of the net.

review.onside_text: The striker is level with or behind your line: ONSIDE.
review.offside_text: The striker is past your line: OFFSIDE.

daylight_robbery.title: Daylight Robbery
daylight_robbery.text: You signal OFFSIDE and the goal is gone. Within minutes, freeze-frames all over the internet show the striker was onside by 30 centimetres. The home fans chant your name in a way you will never forget. PUNDIT: What a call! Clearly offside! ...Right? RIGHT?

clip_of_the_year.title: Clip of the Year
clip_of_the_year.text: You never studied the footage, so you make the call on pure vibes. GOAL! You happen to be right, but the broadcast cuts to your face at the exact moment you decide, and it is not a good face. By morning the clip has 40 million views and its own song. PUNDIT: Absolute cinema. That clip will outlive us all.

right_call_wrong_mouth.title: Right Call, Wrong Mouth
right_call_wrong_mouth.text: Your review was right: onside, the goal stands. But you told the press "Clearly a goal!" before you checked, and now every newspaper says the new VAR official picked a side. You were right, and it does not matter. PUNDIT: Right call, wrong mouth. They'll teach this one at VAR school.

justice_served.title: Justice Served
justice_served.text: Your review settles it: onside, the goal stands. Because you said "No comment", nobody can claim you decided before you checked. The home fans sing your name. The away fans sing something else. The referee gives you a small nod. PUNDIT: Fine. Correct AND professional. Absolutely terrible for my ratings.

var_is_watching.title: VAR Is Watching
var_is_watching.text: You give the goal and the stadium explodes. On every TV in the country, Rex Smugworth freezes mid-grin as two stewards walk into his studio holding a lanyard and a betting slip. In the stands, a pigeon takes off its head and bows. The goal stands. Rex does not. PUNDIT: This is an outrage! I want my lawy-- [SIGNAL LOST]

epilogue: Meanwhile, in the TV studio, Rex Smugworth smooths his hair and smiles. Nobody will ever know who pulled the camera cable at 93:30. Or will they? (Play again to find out.)
